name: ReKep
summary: ReKep represents a task as a sequence of relational constraints among 3D semantic keypoints, each a small Python function returning a cost. A VLM proposes the keypoints and writes the constraints from an image and instruction; a hierarchical solver then optimizes robot actions against them at roughly 10 Hz, supporting multi-stage, bimanual and reactive behaviors without task-specific training.
innovation: Keypoint-relational constraints as a compact, optimizable and VLM-writable task specification.
Real-time constrained optimization closing the loop against a foundation-model-authored objective.
matters: Among the most capable training-free manipulation systems, and readable enough to debug.
limits: Keypoint proposal quality bounds everything; fine force-controlled tasks remain out of reach.
lineage: VoxPoser's value maps replaced by sparser, more structured keypoint constraints.
